text:
Night is a cup of evil. A sharp whistle

from the guard pierces it, like a vibrating pin.

Listen, you, little harlot, how, if you have already gone,

the wave is still black and still makes me burn?


The Earth has coffin edges in the shadow.

Listen, you, little harlot, do not come back.


My flesh swims, swims

in the cup of shadow that still makes me ache;

my flesh swims in it,

as in a swampy woman's heart.


Astral ember... I have felt

dry rubs of clay

fall upon my diaphanous lotus.

Ah, woman! Because of you exists

flesh made of instinct. Ah, woman!


That is why, O black chalice, even though you have already gone,

I choke on dust;

and more desires to drink paw the ground in my flesh!

translation.title: The Black Cup
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the source's pejorative address and dark erotic chalice imagery as historical poetic text.
